articles.title: ISRO Starts Countdown for GSLV-F17 Launch Carrying Advanced EOS-05 Satellite
articles.content: The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) has commenced the 27.5 hour countdown for the GSLV-F17 launch from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota. The 51.7 metre rocket will take off at 02:55 AM IST on September 4. It is going to carry the 2367 kg EOS-05 satellite into orbit. ISRO officials specify that EOS-05 marks a major achievement as the first Earth observation spacecraft from India to be placed in a geosynchronous orbit. It offers near real time imaging to track cyclones, thunderstorms, and natural disasters across India and the neighbouring region. GSLV-F17 Launch Details: Schedule, Payload, and Objectives The GSLV-F17 mission represents the 19th flight of the Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle for India. The rocket will release EOS-05 into a Sub-Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit (Sub-GTO) operating from the Second Launch Pad (SLP). GSLV Latest Mission Parameter Technical Facts Launch Vehicle GSLV-F17 (4m diameter Ogive composite payload fairing) Satellite Payload EOS-05 Earth Observation Satellite (2,367 kg) Target Orbit Sub-Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit (Sub-GTO) Primary Functions Disaster tracking, agricultural monitoring, weather alerts The primary mission goal is to maintain continuous observation over the Indian subcontinent. Data gathered will assist in oceanographic studies, water body tracking, and quick alerts during extreme weather emergencies. GSLV-F17 carrying EOS-05 was moved from the Vehicle Assembly Building (VAB) to the Umbilical Tower (UT) on 28th August 2026 at Satish Dhawan Space Centre, SHAR, Sriharikota, as preparations continue for the scheduled launch on: 🗓️ 04 Sept 2026 | ⏰ 02:55 AM IST Livestreaming… pic.twitter.com/4nW2MUgeYh — ISRO (@isro) September 1, 2026 How Many Stages are There in GSLV? India's Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle uses a complex propulsion framework to lift heavy payloads into high orbits. One of the major queries around ISRO missions , especially this launch, is how many stages are there in GSLV. The GSLV is a 3 stage launch vehicle where - First Stage (GS1) uses a solid rocket motor augmented by four liquid strap on boosters. Second Stage (GS2) is powered by a single liquid-fuel Vikas engine. Third Stage (GS3) utilizes an indigenously developed Cryogenic Upper Stage (CUS) burning liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen. This multi stage design allows the rocket to carry heavy satellites to high altitudes efficiently. GSLV Mk II vs Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle Mark III It is important to distinguish the GSLV configurations used in ISRO's fleet. The GSLV-F17 mission uses the basic GSLV Mk II configuration which features a cryogenic upper stage. The Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle Mark III (now called LVM3) is a heavier lift vehicle capable of launching 4000 kg class payloads to GTO and human spaceflight missions like Gaganyaan. Where to Watch the GSLV-F17 Launch Live Viewers worldwide can watch the GSLV launch live starting at 02:25 AM IST on September 4, 2026. The official live stream will be broadcast on ISRO’s website and its official YouTube channel. You can also watch the launch on DD National. This launch reinforces India's growing space capabilities along with providing key observations to support environmental research and disaster management.

articles.title: Wonderful Raises $550 Million Series C to Scale the AI Operating System for the Enterprise
articles.content: AI Wonderful Raises $550 Million Series C to Scale the AI Operating System for the Enterprise ITN · September 3, 2026 · 4 min read Quick Summary Funding will accelerate product development and global deployment of the Wonderful AI OS, as enterprises move from isolated AI use cases to organization-wide transformation. Mumbai, 3 September, 2026- Wonderful, the AI OS for the enterprise, today announced the closing of… Funding will accelerate product development and global deployment of the Wonderful AI OS, as enterprises move from isolated AI use cases to organization-wide transformation. Mumbai, 3 September, 2026- Wonderful, the AI OS for the enterprise, today announced the closing of a $550 million Series C funding round at a $5B valuation. The round was led by Insight Partners, with participation from Salesforce and existing investors Index Ventures, IVP, Vine Ventures, 9Yards, and Bessemer Venture Partners. Since its Series B in March 2026, Wonderful has expanded its operations to more than 35 markets, grown to 650 employees worldwide, and evolved its platform into a full AI operating system. Customers are now using the Wonderful AI OS to automate end-to-end workflows, build and deploy AI-native applications, and coordinate agents across every part of the enterprise. The funding will accelerate product development, expand Wonderful’s global deployment teams, and support growing enterprise demand for the AI OS. “We’re entering a new era of enterprise transformation,” said Bar Winkler, CEO and co-founder of Wonderful . “Just as cloud platforms became the foundation of the modern enterprise, AI operating systems will become the foundation of every enterprise. Our customers are already proving that once AI reaches production in one part of the business, it quickly expands across the enterprise. Without a shared operating system, AI risks recreating the sprawl of traditional SaaS. Organizations need a shared AI foundation that compounds in value as more of the enterprise relies on it, and that’s exactly what we’re building. This funding allows us to help more enterprises make that transition.” The Wonderful AI OS is the shared operating layer that coordinates agents, workflows, AI-native applications, enterprise context, integrations, and governed execution across the organization. It’s open, model-agnostic and compatible with existing technology stacks, allowing enterprises to adopt new models and capabilities as the industry evolves, without continually rebuilding their stack or becoming dependent on a single provider. Enterprise context, integrations, governance, and reusable capabilities accumulate over time, making every new deployment faster and better governed than the last. The AI OS includes a suite of key products: managed workflows that automate complex end-to-end processes; productivity agents that support employees and improve decision-making; AI-native applications that complement or replace legacy software; and conversational agents that help enterprises serve and grow customers. Products can be deployed independently or combined within the same workflow, with shared governance, security, and orchestration across the platform. “We designed the AI OS to be modular and open because enterprises shouldn’t have to replace everything they already have to become AI-native,” said Roey Lalazar, CTO and Co-founder of Wonderful ....

articles.title: ISRO Set To Launch EOS-05, India's First Geosynchronous Earth Imaging Satellite
articles.content: Sep 03, 2026 | Updated 03:59 PM GMT+5:30 Save & read from anywhere! Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app . The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) is scheduled to launch EOS-05, the country's first Earth observation satellite designed for geostationary orbit, at 2.55 am tomorrow (4 September) from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC) in Sriharikota, Andhra Pradesh. The 2,367-kilogramme spacecraft, also known as GISAT-1A, will be carried by the GSLV-F17 rocket into a sub-geosynchronous transfer orbit before reaching its operational position approximately 36,000 kilometres above the equator. ISRO said that EOS-05 is a state-of-the-art Earth observation spacecraft and the nation's first imaging satellite intended for geosynchronous orbit. Unlike conventional Earth observation satellites that orbit at lower altitudes and pass over regions periodically, this satellite will maintain a fixed position relative to the Earth's rotation, enabling continuous monitoring of the Indian subcontinent and surrounding areas. The satellite is expected to provide near-real-time images at intervals of 30 minutes, with the capability to revisit priority targets every five minutes for rapid observation tasks. This high-frequency imaging capability will support applications including disaster management, agricultural monitoring, environmental assessment, and strategic surveillance, particularly useful during evolving emergencies when agencies require fresh data to make faster decisions. GSLV-F17 represents the 19th flight of India's Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle and marks both a significant advancement in the country's Earth observation capabilities and another test of its indigenous geosynchronous launch technology. The mission serves as a replacement for an identical spacecraft lost in August 2021 when the GSLV-F10 cryogenic upper stage failed to perform as intended during the EOS-03 launch attempt. Following successful deployment, India will join an elite group of nations operating geostationary Earth imaging satellites. articles.title: ISRO to launch Earth observation satellite EOS-05 from Sriharikota tomorrow - Newsonair
articles.content: News On AIR | September 3, 2026 8:24 AM ISRO to launch Earth observation satellite EOS-05 from Sriharikota tomorrow ISRO Chairman V. Narayanan has said that the EOS-05 Earth observation satellite will be launched tomorrow. The satellite is scheduled to lift off at 2:55 AM aboard the GSLV-F17 rocket from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre at Sriharikota. Mr Narayanan said EOS-05 is a state-of-the-art Earth observation spacecraft and India’s first imaging satellite to be placed in a geosynchronous orbit. He said the mission will further strengthen India’s Earth observation capabilities and improve the delivery of Earth observation services. The ISRO Chairman was speaking to the media after offering prayers at the Sri Venkateswara Swamy Temple in Tirumala yesterday. Before offering prayers, Mr Narayanan placed models of the GSLV-F17 rocket at the feet of Lord Venkateswara. He said all arrangements for the launch have been completed at the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota.

articles.title: Uttam Kumar At 100: From Repeated Flops To India's First National Award For Best Actor
articles.content: 152 3rd of September, 2026 marks the 100th birth anniversary of Uttam Kumar, the actor that generations of Bengali moviegoers came to know as nothing else but the “Mahanayak”. However, this nickname was earned hard. Uttam Kumar was once Arun Kumar Chattopadhyay – the man who tried his hand at making his way through the Indian film industry as an aspiring artist. Many of his first movies proved to be failures, and there were plenty of obstacles which could have made any other actor give up. However, he chose not to do so. What followed is one of the most remarkable metamorphoses ever witnessed in Indian cinema, the transformation of a struggling new talent into a romantic idol, respected actor and finally into the first Best Actor award winner at the National Film Awards of India. Who Was Uttam Kumar Before He Became The ‘Mahanayak’? Uttam Kumar was born as Arun Kumar Chattopadhyay on September 3, 1926, in Kolkata. His path into the films was far from easy. He featured in quite a few films, none of which proved to be very successful, and his first stint in the field gave him only limited star value. Nevertheless, Uttam kept working in spite of the failures. This trait of his turned out to be one of the most significant things about him. Even the Prime Minister of India, Mr. Narendra Modi, while paying his tribute before his centenary, talked of this quality of the actor. Which Film Changed Uttam Kumar’s Career? It was in the early 1950s when things really started to change. It was Basu Paribar that helped to draw him into the limelight, but more importantly, there was Sharey Chuattor in 1953. The movie allowed Uttam Kumar to meet Suchitra Sen and the partnership that they formed in this movie would go on to be among the most famous partnerships in Bollywood. Uttam and Suchitra worked together in films like Agni Pariksha, Harano Sur and Saptapadi. They gave birth to a whole new kind of romantic language in Bengali movies. For viewers, the two were not just stars working together in a movie anymore; they had become an emotion. How Did Uttam Kumar Become Bengal’s Biggest Superstar? One of the reasons for the popularity of Uttam Kumar was that he had not used his star power alone. He was a relatively natural actor in his films, especially in a time where acting would be done more dramatically. articles.title: 1939 chargers, 622 km: Kerala's plan for India's first electric truck corridor
articles.content: THIRUVANANTHAPURAM: The Kerala State Electricity Board (KSEB) has proposed developing India’s first electric truck corridor along National Highway 66, with charging facilities planned across the 622-km stretch from Kasaragod to Thiruvananthapuram. The proposal is based on a study conducted by KSEB in collaboration with the International Council on Clean Transportation (ICCT). The study report was released at the India Clean Transport Summit-2026 in New Delhi. The study recommends setting up a charging network with a capacity of 12.5 MW along the corridor. The required funds are expected to come from the Rs 2,000 crore allocated by the Union Ministry of Heavy Industries for public charging infrastructure under the PM E-DRIVE scheme. Kerala can also utilise the Rs 63.12 crore already allocated for a charging network in the State. “By creating India’s first electric truck corridor along National Highway 66, KSEB is demonstrating how the electrification of freight transport can be made practical,” said M.P. Rajan, Director, KSEB Generation and REES Department . 1,939 chargers, 622 km: Kerala’s plan for India’s first electric truck corridor
